research_question: When does an explicit common-phase invariant inductive bias improve ID and channel-OOD receiver performance in SISO and two-layer SU-MIMO?
primary_claim: The invariant receiver improves paired BER and BLER selectively under phase and channel distribution shifts, and the effect depends on the spatial observation dimension.
falsification_criteria: The paired invariant-minus-sensitive effect is non-improving across the declared OOD tests.
Any apparent gain is driven by unequal inputs, training budgets, checkpoint selection, or random samples.
decision_rule: Retain phase invariance only for system and domain cells with a positive paired effect that is stable across declared seeds and is not offset by a material ID regression.

train_domains.description: Extreme-narrow source domain: TDL-A, 10 ns, 200 Hz.
Broad source domain: TDL A-E, 10/30/100/300 ns, 200 Hz.

intentional_differences: SISO uses a Hermitian invariant readout; SU-MIMO uses the phase-canonical receiver.
The phase-sensitive receiver is the parameter-matched control for each system.
